# Actual STM32 TX OOK waveform fixture

`ook_1800_timebase_then_data.mem` is generated by compiling and executing
`Core/Src/fsk_tx.c` against `Tests/hal_mock`; it is not a Python DSP model.
Run `Tests/generate_ook_packet_fixture.ps1` to regenerate it.

Format: one unsigned 12-bit DAC code per line, uppercase hexadecimal, no
address column. Sample rate is 48000 samples/s. OOK one symbols repeat the
exact 80-entry, 3-cycle LUT, therefore carry 1800 Hz; zero and silence symbols
are `800` (decimal 2048). Each air bit is 480 consecutive samples.

The file concatenates two one-shot `MODE PACKET` transmissions with OOK enabled:

1. Time-base packet: sequence 0, V2 type `TIME_BASE`, time `2026-09-23
   00:00:00`, payload length zero by protocol. Its 100 ms pre/post midpoint
   windows are included.
2. Data packet: sequence 0, V2 type `DATA`, elapsed timestamp zero (HAL mock
   tick is fixed), payload `01 23 45 67`, same pre/post midpoint windows.

Generated fixture counts: `time_base_samples=63840`, `data_samples=75360`,
`total_samples=139200`. The first packet starts at sample zero; the second
begins immediately at offset 63840. The generator writes the initial two DMA
halves, then appends each alternately refilled half in callback/render order.
The framing is MSB-first `AAAA 06B7`, unchanged from production TX.

The mock HAL tick is held at zero, so the data-frame elapsed timestamp is zero.
This fixture is the DAC sample stream only; board-level DAC output and physical
pin/channel mapping are supplied separately by the hardware configuration.
